newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Capral sees better prices 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Capral sees better prices 2nd half.

text.p: Capral Aluminium Ltd said on Tuesday that while strong metals prices would underpin the group's second half performance, competitive pressures on the fabricating business would continue.

"These pressures will be offset in part by measures already in place to lift efficiency," Capral chairman Jeremy Davis said in a statement releasing the aluminium refiner and fabricator's first half results.

Capral, formerly known as Alcan Australia Ltd, reported a 0.8 percent fall in net profit to A$17.795 million in the six months to June 30. It set an unchanged interim dividend of eight cents per share.
Capral said the smelting division's earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) rose to A$22.9 million in the first half from A$19.1 million in the same half a year earlier.
Fabrication EBIT fell to A$16.8 million from A$21 million a year earlier because of competitive pressures that increased progressively through the half.

"This resulted in reduced margins from a combination of continuing subdued demand from the building sector, aggressive sales activity from imported product and a consequent inability to pass on LME metal price increases," Capral said. "The erosion in margins has been greatest in the rolling business."
Capral said it was seeking opportunities to expand its extrusion activities in the Asian region.
"Extensive research and analysis of opportunities in the Malaysian, Thai and Indonesian markets has been conducted," it said.
"Whilst there has been some downturn in recent times, particularly in the Thai economy, the company continues to be positive about the long term potential of the region."
Capral Aluminium said cash flow from operations at A$27.6 million for the half meant the balance sheet remained strong with net debt to equity at 30 percent.
Capral's earnings per share fell to 9.6 cents from 9.9 cents per share.
Capral's shares were up 15 cents at A$4.60 by 11.55 a.m. (0155 GMT), implying an annualised price to past earnings ratio of 24.2 times earnings.
